summary: Six scenarios priced end-to-end. THE HEADLINE CORRECTION: the brief's ~$3,100 Zagreb exit estimate is wrong — live ZAG→SFO for 5 is $4,068 (Turkish, 30h25m with a 13.5h overnight IST layover) or $4,452 (Croatia+BA via BRU/LHR, 21h). That single number guts the Zagreb-exit stay-put plan. THE HEADLINE FIND: LHR→SFO is the cheapest exit on the entire board — British Airways NONSTOP, 11h10m, $2,215 for 5 on Nov 2 ($2,358 Nov 1). That beats Prague's $2,365 one-stop, and beats Krakow's $3,379 by $1,164. Because DBV→Stansted is a confirmed 5-seat Ryanair route, every London-exit scenario inherits the cheapest and shortest flight home. Result: the sleeper Jarred suspected IS real, but it's the London-exit version, not the Zagreb one — stay in Dubrovnik all week ($104-135/night live-quoted for 5), fly DBV→STN Nov 1, one London night, BA nonstop home Nov 2: $6,570 total, the cheapest of any Lane 3 ending and by far the lowest effort. Romania ($7,516) and the Krakow+London Ryanair hop ($7,539) land within $25 of each other in the middle — Romania buys Bran Castle on actual Halloween plus a country where Nov 1 is NOT a holiday (everything open while Poland/Austria/Italy shut); the hop buys two genuinely different worlds and dodges the Nov 1 closure problem by relocating to the UK on that exact day. A full London week is $8,698 and lands squarely in half-term (Oct 26-30) — maximum crowds, maximum lodging. Ireland is the most expensive at $9,018 + 81,250 Avios, but it holds the strongest single memory asset in the lane: the Púca Festival (Oct 29 - Nov 1 2026, Trim & Athboy) is Halloween at its literal birthplace, and the Samhain Fire at Tlachtga is free.

options.label: S1b — STAY-PUT SLEEPER: 7 nights Dubrovnik + 1 London night + BA nonstop (CHEAPEST, LOWEST EFFORT)

Sun Nov 1 take Ryanair FR DBV→STN 15:25, arrive 17:35, one night near London, then British Airways LHR→SFO nonstop Nov 2 (11:45 or 15:20 departure, 11h10m). This is the only ending with ONE flight in Europe and a nonstop home. Live Booking.com pull for 5 (4 adults + 1 child, apartments only) Oct 25-31 returned Apartment Tete Mare 3BR $625 total, Apartments Sisic 2BR $809, Dream Estate $1,191 — i.e. $104-135/night. Days: city walls, Srđ cable car, Lokrum island, Cavtat boat, Elafiti islands day trip, Ston oysters + the second-longest wall in Europe (1h drive), Montenegro/Kotor day trip (2h). Downside is honest: they have already had Dubrovnik, and 7 off-season nights in one small walled city is thin for a 16 and 13 year old.

options.label: S2 — TRANSYLVANIA/ROMANIA: Bran Castle on actual Halloween, in the one country where Nov 1 is not a holiday
options.detail: Positioning was never priced at 5 pax — here it is. There is NO Ryanair from Dubrovnik to Romania (DBV→OTP and DBV→CLJ both return zero). The cheapest 5-seat path is DBV→STN Oct 25 15:25 ($503 live, the cheapest exit from Dubrovnik on any day), overnight at a Stansted airport hotel, then Ryanair STN→OTP Oct 26 06:30 ($180 live, €33.17/pp). Pick up an SUV at OTP. Bucharest 2 nights → Brasov 4 nights as the base for Bran, Rasnov and Sinaia → back to Bucharest Nov 1 → British Airways OTP→SFO Nov 2 08:05 via LHR, $3,303 live for 5. BRAN CASTLE HALLOWEEN 2026 IS CONFIRMED AND THERE IS A FAMILY VERSION: the 'New Moon' daytime tour is all-ages, running 09:00-17:00 last admission on Oct 31 itself with amplified effects, actors and dimly-lit corridors. The 800-lei adults-only party (18:00 tour + 21:00-04:00 tent party in the Royal Park) is NOT usable — the 8 and 13 year old are excluded. Exiting from Cluj instead does not solve it: CLJ→SFO live is $4,224, $921 worse than OTP.

options.label: S4 — TWO-CITY RYANAIR HOP (best pairing): Krakow 5 nights + London 2 nights

The winner is Krakow → London, and it wins for a specific reason: it puts the six cheap nights in Krakow ($207/day burn, ~$103/night lodging) and only two expensive nights in London, while still capturing the cheapest exit on the board. Sequence: one extra Dubrovnik night Oct 25 (there is no Oct 25 Krakow flight) → DBV→KRK Mon Oct 26 15:15-16:55 $191 live → Krakow Oct 26-31 → KRK→STN Sat Oct 31 21:40 for €75.96/pp (~$411, live fare-finder) → London Oct 31-Nov 2 → BA LHR→SFO nonstop Nov 2 $2,215. Total air for five: $2,817. Compare with staying in Krakow and exiting there: $191 + $3,379 = $3,570. The hop is $753 cheaper on air AND gives you two cities. Second-order win: it DODGES the Nov 1 closure problem entirely — on the day Wieliczka and half of Krakow shut for All Saints, they are in London where nothing closes, doing the Harry Potter Studio Tour and the Natural History Museum.

Sun Nov 1 is the better Studio Tour day than Sat Oct 31, which is a Saturday inside UK half-term and the single hardest date of the year to get. REJECTED VARIANT — Krakow+Vienna: KRK→VIE Oct 31 22:30 is a steal at EUR32.07/pp (~$173 for 5), but Vienna burn is $500-600/day, Nov 1 IS an Austrian holiday (everything shut), and VIE→SFO is $3,161 — roughly $1,500 worse than the London tail on all three axes.

options.label: S1 — CROATIA STAY-PUT AS BRIEFED: Dubrovnik 6 nights + Zagreb 2 nights, Mirogoj on Nov 1, exit Zagreb
options.detail: This is the scenario exactly as Jarred framed it, and the Mirogoj half of the thesis is fully confirmed: Croatia observes Nov 1 as a public holiday, Mirogoj is the busiest day of its year, thousands of candles light the Central Cross in an effect locals describe as a second sunset visible from a distance, a free shuttle bus runs from near Zagreb Cathedral, and early evening before sundown is the peak moment. Herman Bollé's arcades and cupolas make it a genuine open-air gallery; it sits on the European Cemeteries Route. It is free, it is spectacular, and it is the single best Nov 1 activity found anywhere in this lane. THE PROBLEM IS THE EXIT. The brief's ~$3,100 Zagreb estimate does not survive a live pull. ZAG→SFO Nov 2 for five comes back at $4,068 on Turkish (30h25m with a 13h30m overnight layover in Istanbul — unusable with an 8 year old) or $4,452 on Croatia+British Airways via BRU/LHR (21h, 2 stops). Nov 1 prices identically. That $1,000-1,350 overshoot is what turns the lowest-effort scenario into the fourth-cheapest one.

TIGHT RESCUE VARIANT that keeps Mirogoj and kills the exit premium: Zagreb nights Oct 31 AND Nov 1 (see Mirogoj at dusk Nov 1), then ZAG→STN Nov 2 06:10 (~$621 for 5 based on the live Nov 1 fare of EUR107.39/pp) and BA LHR→SFO Nov 2 15:20 nonstop $2,215. Air becomes $362+$621+$2,215 = $3,198 instead of $4,452+$362 = $4,814 — a $1,616 saving — but it requires a 06:10 departure and a same-day Stansted→Heathrow crossing with five people and bags. I would not run that with an 8 year old unless the savings are decisive. Marked TIGHT, not recommended.

options.label: S3 — LONDON, FULL WEEK
options.detail: DBV→STN Oct 25 15:25 at $503 for five is the cheapest way out of Dubrovnik on any date, and LHR→SFO nonstop at $2,215 is the cheapest way home from anywhere — so London has the best air of any scenario at $2,718 total. Everything else about it is expensive. Live Booking.com for 8 nights sleeping 5: Wimbledon 2BR $1,783, Earls Court 3BR $2,364, and the central options run $3,400-4,500. The window lands squarely inside UK half-term (Oct 26-30) — peak family crowds at every paid attraction and peak lodging. The offsetting virtue is that London's best museums are free: Natural History, Science, British, V&A and Tate Modern all cost nothing, and under-11s ride all TfL free (helps the 8 year old only; the 13 and 16 pay). Harry Potter Studio Tour: Dark Arts confirmed 16 Sep – 8 Nov 2026 and included in standard admission, from £58.50 adult. Oct 31 2026 is a Saturday inside half-term and is realistically the hardest ticket of the year — treat Nov 1 (Sunday) as the target date and book the moment you commit. Tower of London £33.60 adult.

Best projections put Oxford Street around Mon Nov 2 and Regent Street ~Nov 5-6, both evening ceremonies. They fly out Nov 2. They miss it. Do not put this in the pitch. Nov 1 is not a UK holiday, so unlike Poland/Austria/Italy/Spain nothing shuts. Cheapest honest lodging ($1,783 Wimbledon) is a 30-40min commute each way — if you want zone 1-2 add roughly $800-1,200 to this total.

options.label: S5 — IRELAND WEEK WITHOUT DERRY (road trip + Púca Festival + Avios exit)
options.detail: Honest answer to 'is Ireland worth a week on its own': YES for the 16 and 13 year old, marginal for the 8 year old, and it is the most expensive ending in the lane. The thing that makes it worth considering at all is the PÚCA FESTIVAL — confirmed Thu Oct 29 – Sun Nov 1 2026 across Trim and Athboy, Co. Meath (~50 min from Dublin), built by Fáilte Ireland specifically to mark Ireland as the birthplace of Halloween. The Lighting of the Samhain Fire at Tlachtga/Hill of Ward is a FREE public ceremony, the Púca Procession through Trim is free, and Trim Castle gets an audio-visual myth-and-folklore projection installation. That is Halloween at its actual origin point, on the actual date, for free. Headliners under the Big Top (Glen Hansard, The Coronas, Hothouse Flowers) are separately ticketed. Route: DBV→DUB Oct 25 20:40 ($705, the ONLY 5-seat date, which locks the entire week to Ireland), Dublin 2n → Galway 2n (Cliffs of Moher) → Belfast/Antrim 2n (Titanic Belfast, Giant's Causeway) → Meath/Dublin 2n (Púca) → Aer Lingus EI61 DUB→SFO ~13:00 Nov 2 on Avios.
options.points_cost: 81,250 Avios (16,250/pp × 5) + $973.15 cash fees ($194.63/pp). 6+ award seats verified on BOTH Nov 1 and Nov 2. Cash alternative if you would rather keep the Avios: $2,757 for 5 via LHR on Nov 1 (Aer Lingus+BA, 14h10m) or $3,418 for the EI nonstop — using the award saves $1,784-2,445 in cash.

Nights: 8n across Dublin/Galway/Belfast/Meath $2,340. Activities $700. Daily burn $3,200 (8 days @ ~$400, self-catering assumed). Exit: EI61 DUB→SFO award fees $973 (plus 81,250 Avios).

options.notes: WHY IT COSTS THE MOST: the $400/day Irish burn is the second-highest in the lane and it runs for all eight days, unlike London where only 2 days do in the hop scenario. DRIVING LOAD IS REAL: Dublin→Galway 2.5h, Galway→Causeway ~4.5h, Causeway→Trim ~3h — 12+ hours behind the wheel on the left in eight days. The 8 year old will fade on those days. IRISH RENTAL GOTCHA: Irish agencies are notoriously strict about credit-card CDW — one traveller reported an $8,600 hold. Either buy the agency's own zero-excess coverage (priced in above) or bring a printed letter of coverage naming Ireland. Also note a 'seven-seater' in Ireland often means seven seats OR luggage space, rarely both — check boot capacity with all seats up or take a 9-seater. Castle stay is NOT included: Ashford/Kilkea are luxury tier; the realistic budget version is Clontarf Castle Hotel Dublin at roughly $400/night for five across two rooms — add $400 for one night if you want it. Big Top Púca headliner tickets would add ~$300 for five.

caveats: PRICE CONFIDENCE, honestly labelled. (1) Every long-haul exit fare in this lane was pulled live from Google Flights on 2026-08-02 at TRUE 5-passenger pricing (4 adults + 1 child, since Google classes 13 and 16 as adults and 8 as a child) — ZAG→SFO, OTP→SFO, CLJ→SFO, LHR→SFO Nov 1 and Nov 2, DUB→SFO. Those are the most reliable numbers here. (2) Every lodging figure was pulled live from Booking.com on 2026-08-02 with the same 4+1 party and filtered to apartments — Dubrovnik, Zagreb, Krakow, London (8-night and 2-night), Dublin, Galway, Bucharest, Brasov. Also reliable, but rates 15 months out are volatile and inventory is thin; re-pull in early 2026. (3) Ryanair intra-Europe hop fares came from the Ryanair fare-finder API, which returns the CHEAPEST fare bucket for ONE passenger. Five seats at that exact fare are NOT verified — assume real-world 5-pax pricing lands 15-40% higher on the tighter routes. Every Ryanair-dependent total carries an added bags-and-seats line ($180 for one sector, $300-350 for two) because Ryanair base fares exclude checked luggage and a family of five that does not pay for seat assignment will be split up. (4) Daily-burn figures are modelled, not quoted — I used the brief's verified Krakow $207 and Dublin $400-480 as anchors, and derived Croatia ~$200, Romania ~$173 and London ~$320 from 2026 cost guides. Burn is the single softest line in every total. THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF. First: the ~$3,100 Zagreb exit estimate is wrong — live is $4,068 (30h25m, unusable layover) to $4,452 (21h). Second: Auschwitz-Birkenau is OPEN on Nov 1 (it closes only Jan 1, Dec 25 and Easter Sunday) — the Nov 1 shutdown rule does not apply to it, though Wieliczka's closure stands. Third: Romania does not observe Nov 1 as a public holiday, so it is the only country in this lane where a full Nov 1 of open museums and castles is available. FOUR THINGS I WILL NOT SELL. London's Christmas lights switch-on is ~Nov 2-6 2026, unannounced, evening ceremonies — they are on a plane, they miss it. NOX at the Harry Potter Studio Tour is 16+ and excludes the 8 year old. The Bran Castle adults-only Halloween party (800 lei) excludes the 8 and 13 year old — only the all-ages 'New Moon' daytime tour works. HiSky's OTP→JFK nonstop is unverified for winter 2026 (schedule loaded only through spring 2026, widebody shifting to a new Bucharest–Chicago route) — do not plan a Romania exit around it. TWO OPEN ITEMS NEEDING A LIVE BOOKING-ENGINE CHECK BEFORE ANY OF THIS IS COMMITTED: Harry Potter Studio Tour actual seat availability for 5 on Oct 31 and Nov 1 2026 (the calendar sits behind a booking widget I could not query; Oct 31 is a Saturday in UK half-term and is the likeliest sell-out date of the year), and true 5-seat Ryanair availability at the quoted fares on KRK→STN Oct 31 and DBV→STN Nov 1. Raw pull artifacts are at /tmp/lane3/ (out_*.json for flights, bk_*.json for lodging) — worth committing under /Users/jarredwinn/.omnara/worktrees/miscellaneous/wasabi-discern/data/raw/lane3-wildcards/ alongside the lane1 and lane2 pulls.

=== (2) FLYING BLUE AWARD SPACE: WHAT IS FINDABLE = NOTHING ===

METHODOLOGY NOTE WORTH KNOWING: I decoded the Google Flights tfs parameter and confirmed the passenger field is [1,1,1,1,2] = four adult-rate passengers plus one child. That is correct for this family — a 16- and a 13-year-old price as adults on essentially every carrier; only the 8-year-old is a child. My encoder reproduces the original captured URL byte-identically, so these pulls are the same query shape as the earlier verified data, not a different search. All prices shown are TOTALS for the party of five, which is how Google Flights displays multi-passenger fares.

ESTIMATED, NOT VERIFIED — and these are where the totals can move:
- London nightly burn ($500/day for five). This is the single softest number in the analysis and it drives the London options directly. Not in your verified burn list.
- Flying Blue award taxes and surcharges (~$220/pp economy, ~$280/pp premium economy). Real figures could run higher from some origins.
- Krakow->Prague surface transfer (~$200/5). FlixBus would likely be cheaper, rail dearer.
- LHR->DUB positioning (~$250/5) — I did not pull this one; it only appears in a comparison I concluded against anyway.
- Activity budgets ($300-400) are placeholders, not researched for this lane.

THE ONE THING I WOULD NOT GUESS AT: Flying Blue 5-seat saver availability. I made three separate attempts (raw HTTP, headless browser, and the free explore page) and it is genuinely not obtainable without a login — seats.aero search returns Cloudflare 403 even to a real browser, and the free explore window does not reach 91 days out. On top of that seats.aero currently displays a banner saying its Flying Blue data is recovering from an outage. Any FB number I gave you is a PRICE, not a PROMISE of space. The Aer Lingus EI61 award is the opposite: 6+ seats verified on both Nov 1 and Nov 2, and it is the only award in this entire matrix you can actually plan around.

ONE HONEST TENSION IN THE RECOMMENDATION: whether the points are "worth it" depends entirely on which cash baseline you measure against, and both readings are defensible. Against each city's own fare, the awards look good (Krakow 1.92c, Dublin/Avios 2.25c). Against the best ending you could actually book — Krakow base with a London exit at $4,832 — every single redemption falls below your 1.54 floor (Avios 1.34c, FB saver 1.47c, promo premium economy 1.02c). I lean toward the second reading because you are free to choose the cheap exit, but I am flagging it rather than burying it, because the first reading is what a points blog would tell you and it is not wrong, just anchored to a fare you do not have to pay.

FINALLY, ON THE AUGUST PROMO: it is real and it is confirmed, but I could not confirm the Europe->SFO direction specifically. Award options carry a separate points_cost and I state the points-valued total (at a conservative 1.5¢/MR) in each detail field. (2) THE SINGLE BIGGEST UNVERIFIED VARIABLE is Flying Blue 5-seat saver space ex-KRK (and ex-anywhere) on Nov 1. Verify this before choosing the Krakow shape at all, because the Krakow CASH exit (SAS $3,379) is the most expensive exit on the board and routing yourself there on spec is the one genuinely expensive mistake available in Lane 1. By contrast the Aer Lingus EI61 path is verified at 6+ seats on BOTH Nov 1 and Nov 2, and Prague's $2,365 BA fare is a confirmed cash number — those two are the de-risked exits.

(3) WHAT IS LIVE vs ESTIMATED. Live-quoted at true 5-passenger pricing this session: RegioJet Wien→Praha all four Oct 25 departures (€64.50 / €179.50 ×3) and the Oct 26–28 grid; RegioJet Kraków→Praha and Praha→Kraków directs (€89.50–114.50); Booking.com Prague 6-night and Zakopane 3-night inventory; Ryanair fare grids for DBV→VIE, KRK→DUB, PRG→DUB. Calibrated: Ryanair 5-pax pricing — I validated that lead-in fare × 5 reproduces the verified DBV→KRK $191 almost exactly (€33.17 × 5 = €165.85 = $191 at today's 1.1538), so I applied lead-in × 5 to KRK→DUB and PRG→DUB. FX from live pull 2026-08-03: EUR $1.1538, PLN $0.2677, CZK $0.0477.

(4) CLOSURE AND AGE FLAGS THAT CHANGE ITINERARIES. Wieliczka is CLOSED Nov 1 — schedule Oct 26–31. Auschwitz recommends 14+, which is why every Krakow scenario prices it as a 3-person split day, and from March 1 2026 ALL entry passes must be pre-booked online with no walk-up whatsoever. Rynek Underground is free on Tuesdays but only 10:00–14:00 with same-day box-office pickup — Oct 27 is your Tuesday. Kraków's Dragon's Den is seasonal and commonly shuts around end of October; treat its $16 as optional. Kasprowy Wierch cable car (the whole snow proposition in scenario 2) uses timed tickets that sell out and has taken late-October maintenance closures in past years. In Czechia, Oct 28 IS a public holiday (Independence Day — retail closed, Castle open with special programming) while Nov 1 is NOT, the reverse of Poland.

(5) DAILY BURN is food, local transit, and incidentals only — lodging and activities are separate line items in every breakdown, so do not double-count. I charged one burn-day per night, plus one Dubrovnik dead-day burn ($220) in every scenario that requires the Oct 25 Dubrovnik night.

(6) I did not re-derive any of the pre-supplied verified facts, and I resurrected nothing from the dead list.

summary:
FOUR THINGS THE LIVE PULLS CHANGED, before the options.

(1) DBV→BUDAPEST DOES NOT EXIST IN THE WINDOW. Ryanair's own timetable API returns an EMPTY schedule for DBV→BUD for both October and November 2026. The route is summer-seasonal (Jun 2 – Sep 29 2026, Mon/Fri/Sun); Wizz's competing BUD-DBV also launched Jun 8 seasonal. Budapest must be reached overland. Dead, confirmed at the source.

(2) DBV→VIENNA FLIES ON OCT 25 ITSELF, AT 10:00. Ryanair FR9756 (Lauda Europe), DBV 10:00 → VIE 11:25, live Basic Fare €50.99 pp = €254.95/5 ≈ $278 base (the supplied $295 is consistent once seat/fee is added). Full Oct/Nov schedule pulled: Oct 25 10:00, Oct 27 17:20, Oct 30 21:35, Nov 1 10:00 (€48.44 pp, page shows "5 seats left at this price" — 5-pax availability positively confirmed on Nov 1). This is the single biggest unlock in Lane 2: they can leave Dubrovnik on checkout day, land in Vienna before noon, and be in Budapest by ~17:40 the same day via Railjet. No wasted night, no Zagreb detour.

(3) THE ZAGREB AND LJUBLJANA EXITS ARE ~$1,100–1,600 WORSE THAN THE WORKING ESTIMATE. Live Google Flights, 5 pax one-way: ZAG→SFO Nov 1 = $4,178 (Turkish, 30h25 with a 13h30 Istanbul layover) / $4,689 for the sane 19h Croatia+BA via ZRH+LHR. LJU→SFO Nov 1 = $4,564 (Turkish, 30h50) / Nov 2 $4,672–4,788 (two stops FRA+SEA, 18–20h); the 1-stop Lufthansa/United via FRA is $9,001. The "Zagreb ~$3,100 est" does not survive contact. This is what breaks Slovenia's economics, not Slovenia itself.

(4) THE "VIENNA IS 2.5x KRAKOW" PREMISE DOES NOT SURVIVE LIVE LODGING. I pulled Booking.com apartments for exactly 2 adults + children 16/13/8, price-sorted. Vienna Oct 25→Nov 1 (7 nights, 5 pax): floor $456 for a 3-bedroom, working band $476–503 — that is $65–72/NIGHT FOR FIVE. Budapest Oct 26→Nov 1 (6 nights): floor $393 for a 3-bedroom, band $470–495 = $65–83/night. Vienna beds are NOT more expensive than Budapest beds, and both quoted CHEAPER per night than the Krakow figure supplied ($607–796 / 6 nights = $101–133/night). The real Vienna premium is food and paid admissions, roughly +40% on the food line. All-in with a kitchen, Vienna runs ~$361/day for five, not $500–600. I am flagging rather than overwriting: every Vienna option below carries BOTH my live-lodging-anchored number and the supplied hotel/restaurant-tier number so you can pick which model you believe.

TWO ATTRACTION RETRACTIONS YOU ASKED FOR BY NAME:
• GELLÉRT BATHS ARE CLOSED. Shut Oct 1 2025 for renovation, reopening planned 2028. Confirmed by a Jun 2026 update. There is no Gellért on this trip.
• SZÉCHENYI HAS A HARD AGE-14 MINIMUM. The 13-year-old and the 8-year-old cannot enter the thermal pools — not a guideline, a rule, and Rudas bars under-14s from the complex entirely. Under-14s may only use an indoor swimming pool if they can swim. So "Széchenyi + Gellért thermal baths family tickets" is a two-way dead end: one bath is closed, the other splits your family 3-and-2. The genuine family substitute is PALATINUS STRAND on Margaret Island — open year-round, indoor thermal + kids' pool running Sep–May, winter hours ~09:00–16:00 from about Oct 21 — but the big slides and wave pool are closed in winter. Budget it as a nice indoor swim, not a Széchenyi replacement.

WHAT SURVIVED VERIFICATION AND IS GENUINELY GOOD:
• AUSTRIAN NATIONAL DAY, MON OCT 26 — REAL AND FREE. Federal museums free (Kunsthistorisches, Naturhistorisches, Weltmuseum), the entire Austrian National Library group free all day (Prunksaal, Globe, Papyrus, Esperanto, House of Austrian History), plus the Heldenplatz ceremony and the Armed Forces display with the Chancellery/Parliament/Hofburg open to the public. Worth $150–200 of admissions to this party, and it lands the day after a Oct 25 arrival. Caveat: it is a public holiday, so shops are shut and restaurants thin. Albertina is private and NOT included.
• VIENNALE OCT 22 – NOV 3 2026 — CONFIRMED, 64th edition, covers the entire window. ~300 films, tickets ~€11–14. Be honest about who it is for: it is an art-house festival for the adults and maybe the 16-year-old, not a family activity. A 2025-introduced "Young Audience" strand is the only kid hook.
• POSTOJNA IS THE BEST SINGLE KID ATTRACTION IN THIS ENTIRE LANE. Answering your question directly: yes, genuinely top-tier, and it is not close. You board an open electric train and ride ~2 km INTO the mountain through lit galleries before an hour on foot — a cave railway running since 1872, unique at this scale — then the Vivarium with live Proteus anguinus, blind cave salamanders that live ~100 years and can go a decade without eating, which every kid on earth calls baby dragons. Pair it with Predjama Castle, a fortress built into a cliff cave mouth. For an 8-year-old this beats anything in Vienna or Budapest on wow-per-euro. Live low-season pricing (Oct–May): adult €27.90, student €22.90, child 6–15 €18.90; Cave+Castle combo €40.30 adult (~10% off). Late-Oct tours: first 10:00, LAST 14:00, every 2 hours — a short window, plan the day around it. Open every day of the year including holidays. Cave is 10°C; bring jackets. The train does not wait for latecomers.
• SLOVENIA HAS TWO CONSECUTIVE WORK-FREE HOLIDAYS AT THE END OF YOUR WINDOW: Sat Oct 31 (Reformation Day) and Sun Nov 1 (Day of Remembrance for the Dead). Expect shops and supermarkets closed both days, heavy cemetery traffic. A self-catering family of five must stock up by Fri Oct 30. Postojna itself stays open. Nov 1 is also a holiday in Hungary, Austria and Croatia — but NOT in Czechia, which quietly favors the Prague exit.
• BUDAPEST ZOO HALLOWEEN: format is real and excellent (fire jugglers, pumpkin carving, candle trail, bravery tests, costumed under-14s historically entering for a symbolic 200–500 HUF), typically the last Friday of October — which would be Oct 30 2026, inside your window. But the 2026 date is NOT posted by the zoo yet. Unverified; do not build the trip around it.

THE MOVE I WOULD PUT IN FRONT OF EVERYTHING ELSE: Flying Blue works from BOTH Vienna and Budapest, and the August promo is the whole ballgame. KLM operates BUD→AMS→SFO in 14h15 with a 1h05 AMS connection and VIE→AMS→SFO in 13h55 with a 1h00 connection — both live-confirmed daily, both the SHORTEST routings available and 2.5 hours faster than the BA-via-LHR fares below. At 30,000/pp PREMIUM ECONOMY that is 150,000 MR out of a ~525,000 pool — 29% of the pool converts a $2,953–$3,240 cash exit into premium economy seats plus ~$350 in taxes. Ljubljana is the exception: its only KLM timing carries a 19h AMS layover, so FB does not rescue the Slovenia lane. 5-seat saver space remains UNVERIFIED and Flying Blue reprices the entire party to flex if fewer than 5 saver seats exist — check this before anything else, because it reorders every option below.

caveats:
WHAT IS LIVE vs WHAT IS ESTIMATED — read before quoting any of these numbers back.

LIVE-PULLED TODAY (high confidence): every SFO exit fare (Google Flights, 5 passengers, one-way, USD); every lodging floor and band (Booking.com, price-sorted, configured as 2 adults + children aged 16/13/8, entire-apartment filter); the Ryanair DBV→VIE fare (€50.99 pp Oct 25, €48.44 pp Nov 1 with "5 seats left at this price" shown); every Ryanair DBV schedule for Oct–Nov 2026 pulled from Ryanair's own timetable API; Postojna's low-season price list and late-October tour window; Schönbrunn Zoo's 2A+3C family ticket at €96.

ESTIMATED BY ME, NOT QUOTED (treat as ±25%): all food and local-transit daily figures ($150 Budapest, $215 Vienna, $190 Slovenia); the Budapest→Prague transfer ($150); the Prague night ($120); the Slovenian car all-in ($598); activity bundles as totals. I have labeled the option-level price_confidence to the weakest major input, not the strongest.

RYANAIR BAGGAGE IS NOT IN THE $295. Five people on a nine-day trip will check bags; three 20kg checked bags run roughly €35–60 each, about $165 total, and it applies to every option that uses the DBV→VIE flight (1B, 1C, 2, 4, 4C). Croatia Airlines DBV→ZAG typically includes a checked bag, which narrows the gap between 1A and 1B by more than the fare difference suggests. Ryanair also requires an accompanying adult to buy a reserved seat when travelling with a child under 12 — the 8-year-old forces roughly $15 of seat fees.

RYANAIR'S 5-PAX AVAILABILITY API REFUSED ME. The booking availability endpoint returned HTTP 409 "Availability declined" on every attempt, so I could not machine-verify seat counts at 5 the way you did for the other routes. What I have instead is the booking page itself rendering a live per-person fare for a 3-adult + 1-teen + 1-child party, and the Nov 1 page explicitly displaying "5 seats left at this price." I did not extrapolate that to Oct 25 — the Oct 25 page showed no seats-left warning at all, which usually means ample inventory, but I am telling you it is an inference rather than a confirmation.

THE $2,887 BUDAPEST FIGURE ON RECORD IS SLIGHTLY OPTIMISTIC BUT ESSENTIALLY RIGHT. My live pull returns $2,953 for the good Nov 2 itinerary (BA 07:20 → 14:55, 16h35, 2h15 LHR). There is a $2,918 Finnair fare via Helsinki and Dallas, but it is 33h08. And there is a $2,953 fare on Nov 1 that looks identical on price and is 29h10 with a 15h15 Heathrow layover — the trap is that the two Nov 1/Nov 2 fares are the same money for wildly different days. Book Nov 2.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY AND WOULD CHECK NEXT, in priority order: (1) Flying Blue 5-seat saver space at 30,000/pp premium economy from BUD and VIE — this single check reorders the entire lane and the promo dies Aug 31, so it is genuinely urgent; (2) the Budapest Zoo Halloween 2026 date, likely Fri Oct 30 but unposted; (3) whether the Postojna–Predjama shuttle runs in late October, which decides whether the Slovenia car is optional; (4) Vintgar Gorge's 2026 closing date; (5) live ÖBB Sparschiene availability on the specific Railjet departures — the €19.90 fare is limited-inventory and the free-child rule only attaches to Sparschiene tickets, so if it sells out the VIE→BUD leg jumps from $81 to as much as $263 at the walk-up rate.

ONE STRUCTURAL POINT ABOUT THE 16-YEAR-OLD. He is an adult to Ryanair (16+), an adult to ÖBB's free-child rule (which only covers under-15s), a child to Schönbrunn Zoo (6–18, so the €96 family ticket works), and a student to Postojna at €22.90 if he carries ID. That inconsistency is worth $50–80 across the trip and is the kind of thing that silently breaks a booking if someone assumes "three kids" throughout.
